headline: Graph and partition methods for single-cell and spatial multi-omic data analysis
label: Graph Based Single Cell Spatial
summary: Graph-based methods now integrate paired single-cell multi-omics and score spatial transcriptomic clustering quality, alongside a new spatial co-occurrence…
synthesis: The common thread is graph-based computational structure imposed on single-cell and spatial data, with each item representing relationships among cells, labels, or spatial categories as a graph or partition. bionSBM applies graph-based topic modelling to paired single-cell multi-omic profiles from CITE-seq, SHARE-seq, and 10X Multiome data to support clustering and interpretation. CEMUSA addresses evaluation rather than inference, combining label agreement, spatial organization, and error severity into one metric for spatial transcriptomics clustering. The partition-based spatial entropy RCE quantifies category co-occurrences that depend on local environment, applied to immune cells around amyloid plaques. What is new across these items is the explicit use of graph or partition structure to capture spatial context and label relationships, with each method targeting a distinct stage: integration, evaluation, and spatial co-occurrence.
